en.title: Familiar and formal you
en.summary: English has a single word for you, both familiar and formal.

paragraphs: Many languages have one word for you to a friend and another for you to a stranger or an older person. English has only one: you. It is used for one person or for many, and for family, friends and strangers alike. Politeness is shown by other means.

English once had thou for the familiar singular, but it left everyday speech long ago. Today we show politeness with titles, modal verbs and set phrases. Words such as could, would and might make a request more polite. The words please and thank you are very frequent.

blocks.html:
SituationPolite choice
askingCould you help me, please?
offeringWould you like some tea?
addressingMr Brown, Ms Clark
interruptingExcuse me, ...
refusingI'm afraid I can't.

paragraphs: To make clear that you means several people, many speakers say you all, you guys, y'all or you lot. These forms depend on region and register. In writing, the neutral you all is always safe.
The level is set by the words around you, not by you. Hey, can you help? is casual. Would you be so kind as to help? is very formal. Both use the same word you.

items: Wrong: **Give me water.** (to a stranger) Right: **Could I have some water, please?**
Wrong: **Thou art right.** (today) Right: **You are right.**
Wrong: **You is right.** Right: **You are right.**

ro.title: Tu și dumneavoastră
ro.summary: În limba română folosim „tu” pentru prieteni și „dumneavoastră” pentru a vorbi politicos cu persoane necunoscute.

paragraphs: În limba română avem două moduri principale de adresare directă. Când vorbim cu un prieten sau cu un copil, folosim pronumele „tu”. Când vorbim cu un adult necunoscut, folosim pronumele de politețe „dumneavoastră”.

Pronumele „tu” se folosește cu verbul la persoana a doua singular. Pronumele „dumneavoastră” se folosește întotdeauna cu forma de plural a verbului. Această formă de politețe este identică pentru o singură persoană sau pentru mai multe persoane.
